2. When buffer is not full, calculate average of available samples only (no zero padding)
3. When full, use FIFO to replace oldest sample
4. Output sampleCount (0..8)
5. windowFull becomes TRUE when 8 samples are accumulated
6. When enable is FALSE, clear buffer but keep filteredValue

FUNCTION_BLOCK FB
VAR_INPUT
    enable      : BOOL;
    rawValue    : REAL;
END_VAR

VAR_OUTPUT
    filteredValue : REAL;
    windowFull    : BOOL;
    sampleCount   : INT;
END_VAR

VAR
    buffer      : ARRAY[0..7] OF REAL;  // Circular buffer for 8 samples
    writeIndex  : INT := 0;              // Next write position
    prev_enable : BOOL := FALSE;         // Previous enable state
END_VAR

// Implementation logic here
```

Let me think through the logic:

1. When enable is FALSE:
   - Clear buffer (sampleCount = 0)
   - windowFull = FALSE
   - filteredValue keeps last value

2. When enable is TRUE:
   - If transitioning from FALSE to TRUE (rising edge on enable), reset buffer
   - If buffer not full (sampleCount < 8), add new value and increment count
   - If buffer full (sampleCount = 8), overwrite oldest value using circular buffer

   - Update windowFull flag

FUNCTION_BLOCK FB
VAR_INPUT
    enable      : BOOL;
    rawValue    : REAL;
END_VAR

    sampleCount   : INT;
END_VAR

    // Increment sample count if buffer not yet full
